audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven side tokens disagreed with their own explanation. whys[1] and whys[2] describe Graves' burst window ('your cleanest kill window of the lane') but both read Skill; whys[3] literally says 'it's a coin-flip skirmish' but read Graves; whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] all describe Trundle taking over but read Skill, Skill and Graves.
audit.why: The packet chart — Skill / Graves / Graves / Skill / Trundle / Trundle / Trundle — matches the written reasoning. Subjugate steals health, armor and MR and the amount doubles over four seconds, so a drain tank with two items simply cannot be duelled by a champion whose defence is stacked resists.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet in both layers, phase whys rewritten to match, and the rating brought in line: 'Favoured 4/10' is not defensible against a chart that gives Trundle the last three stages and a 45% win rate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was rated a Graves stage in the full layer ('Collateral Damage adds an execute and a disengage knockback'), and Subjugate's cooldown appeared nowhere despite being named the matchup-defining ability on five fields.
audit.why: Subjugate is 650 range on 120/100/80s and its steal doubles over four seconds. Level 6 is Trundle's spike, not Graves' — and the thing that makes it his is that True Grit's stacked resists are the resource it takes.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Trundle with the resist-steal stated; cooldown and range written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields tell you to 'W-blind his Chomp auto' — whys[2], early and wants.you[0].
audit.why: Two errors stacked: Graves' Smoke Screen has no blind at all ('reduces sight range... Move Speed reduced briefly'), and Chomp is a targeted cast — 'Trundle bites his opponent' — so it could not be made to miss even if the blind existed. The Trundle-side audit corrected the same claim from his perspective.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten, with Chomp's 3.5s cooldown given so the AD-sap pressure is concrete instead of vague.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice was mentioned only as something that 'walls off your escape lines', with no cooldown, and King's Tribute never appears at all.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice is 1000 range on 21/19.5/18/16.5/15s and creates impassable terrain — that is the ability that denies Quickdraw, and knowing it is a 15-21s commitment tells you whether to dash. King's Tribute heals him for a percent of the maximum health of any enemy unit that dies near him, which is why he never has to leave a lane he is losing.
audit.corrected: Pillar's range and cooldown added to mid; King's Tribute added to early.

edits.before: Trundle is one of the rare melee laners who actually wants you in his face. Your level 2-3 window is real — E in, W-blind a Chomp (Q) auto, and burst him point-blank with your shell spread plus the End of the Line cone before his bite has stolen enough AD to swing the trade. But every Chomp he lands rips attack damage off you and hands it to him, so your damage bleeds out fast the longer you stand and auto-fight. Hit your combo, deal it in one burst, then E out — do not brawl a champion built to win the long fight.
edits.after: Trundle is one of the rare melee laners who actually wants you in his face. Your level 2-3 window is real — E in and burst him point-blank with your shell spread plus the End of the Line cone before his bite has stolen enough AD to swing the trade. Smoke Screen will not help there: it has no blind, and Chomp is a targeted cast on 3.5 seconds that cannot miss. Every Chomp rips attack damage off you, and King's Tribute heals him off every minion that dies nearby, so the long fight is always his. Burst once, then E out.

edits.before: From level 6 the lane tips against you. Subjugate (R) steals a percent of your armor and magic resist and heals him off the stolen stats — so the exact True Grit stacking that beats other bruisers becomes his fuel, and the deeper you commit the more he strips. His Pillar (E) walls off your Quickdraw escape lines, and Frozen Domain (W) lets him chase or peel through your Smoke Screen. Your burst still hurts, but a Trundle with R up out-sustains it — only commit when his R is down, and even then bait the Pillar before you dash.
edits.after: From level 6 the lane tips against you. Subjugate (R) steals a percent of your health, armor and magic resist and the amount doubles over four seconds — so the exact True Grit stacking that beats other bruisers becomes his fuel, and the deeper you commit the more he strips. Pillar of Ice (E, 1000 range, 15-21s) is impassable terrain that walls off your Quickdraw lines, and Frozen Domain gives him the move speed to chase through your Smoke Screen slow. Commit only when his R is down, and bait the Pillar before you dash.

edits.before: Win the level 2-3 window: E in, W-blind his Chomp auto, and burst point-blank with Q before his bite shaves your AD
edits.after: Win the level 2-3 window: E in and burst point-blank with Q before Chomp's 3.5s bite starts shaving your AD off

notes: Six of seven chart stages argued against their own whys, and the page was rated 'Favoured 4/10' while its own late-game text says you cannot 1v1 him — both fixed. The blind claim appears here in its weakest form: Chomp is a targeted cast, so even a real blind could not make it miss, and Graves has no blind to begin with. Best additions: Subjugate's steal doubling over four seconds (which is why a long duel is worse than it looks), Pillar of Ice's 1000 range and 15-21s as the thing that actually denies Quickdraw, and King's Tribute healing him off nearby minion deaths.
